scenes.headline: How one weight read commits several tokens
scenes.sub: Two one-person engines: TensorFold on a Mac, Strata on a 12 GB GPU.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cumin! Two one-person engines claim big speedups. Both read the weights once and keep several tokens.

scenes.text: Draft a few tokens cheaply, verify them all in one pass over the weights, and keep every one the model agrees with.
scenes.mark: verify them all in one pass
scenes.say: Decoding speed is bytes read per token. So draft a few tokens, check them all in one pass, and keep the matches.

scenes.title: TensorFold: one pass, a tree of drafts

steps.say: A small drafter proposes candidates, and TensorFold grows a tree of up to fifteen of them.
The tree goes through the twenty-seven billion target as sixteen rows of one pass.
Noise keyed to the seed and position means a draft survives only if serial decoding would pick it too.

scenes.title: One forward pass of the 27B
scenes.say: Extra rows must be nearly free. The lane kernel's sixteen rows cost barely more than one. MLX's own kernel more than triples.

scenes.title: Strata: one layer, three workers
scenes.say: Strata fits a hundred and twenty-five billion parameter model onto a twelve gigabyte card.

items.say: The GPU runs the dense weights and the router.
Cached experts run on the GPU.
The CPU computes the misses in system memory.
The next layer waits for the slower half.

steps.say: VRAM holds the dense weights and the hottest experts.
System RAM holds every expert, pinned.
The SSD keeps the n-gram table.

scenes.label: of routed experts per token, 2% of the arena
scenes.note: Q2_0 file, recomputed from the expert shapes
scenes.say: Each token reads about two thirds of a gigabyte of experts. PCIe alone could never carry sixty-five tokens a second.

left.title: Dense model, fast memory
left.say: In a dense model, an extra draft rides along almost free.

right.title: Offloaded mixture of experts
items: Each token brings its own experts
right.say: Offloaded, every extra token drags its own experts down the slow path.

scenes.text: Speed is bytes per committed token. Dense models want more tokens per pass; offloaded experts want more cache hits.
scenes.say: Remember: speed is bytes per committed token. Dense models want tokens per pass. Offloaded experts want VRAM.

recap: One pass verifies many drafted tokens
Row-invariant kernels keep the output exact
Experts in VRAM decide offloaded speed
scenes.say: One pass, many tokens. Exact kernels, same text. And VRAM decides offloaded speed.
